ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, a wooden board B of mass m is placed on horizontal ground, and a wooden box A also of mass m is placed on wooden board B. One end of a light rope is tied to the wooden box, and the other end is tied to a wooden stake on the ground; when the rope is taut, the angle with the horizontal plane is $\theta$. It is known that the coefficient of kinetic friction between wooden box A and wooden board B, and the coefficient of kinetic friction between wooden board B and the ground, are both $\mu$. Now a horizontal force F is used to pull wooden board B out from under wooden box A at uniform speed. Find the expression for the magnitude of the horizontal pulling force $F$.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, wooden board B is placed on rough horizontal ground, and wooden box A is placed on wooden board B; the left side of wooden box A is connected to a light rope, and the light rope is connected obliquely downward to the left to a wooden stake on the ground, with the angle between the rope and the horizontal plane marked as θ; the right side of wooden board B is subjected to a horizontal rightward pulling force F. From the direction of the pulling force shown in the figure, it can be known that B is pulled out to the right at uniform speed, and A has a tendency to slide leftward relative to B, so the sliding friction force exerted by B on A is to the right; the tension exerted by the rope on A is along the rope obliquely downward to the left, with components Tcosθ horizontally to the left and Tsinθ vertically downward. Reasoning: Let the rope tension be T, and the normal force between A and B be N_A. For the force equilibrium of wooden box A: in the horizontal direction, Tcosθ = μN_A; in the vertical direction, N_A = mg + Tsinθ. Combining gives Tcosθ = μ(mg + Tsinθ), that is, T(cosθ - μsinθ)=μmg, so T=μmg/(cosθ-μsinθ). Substituting back into N_A=mg+Tsinθ gives N_A=mg cosθ/(cosθ-μsinθ). Analyze wooden board B: the friction force exerted by A on B is to the left, with magnitude μN_A; the friction force exerted by the ground on B is also to the left, with magnitude μN_g. The normal force exerted by the ground on B is equal to B's own weight plus the pressure exerted by A on B, namely N_g=mg+N_A. B moves at uniform speed, and the horizontal resultant force is zero, so F=μN_A+μN_g=μN_A+μ(mg+N_A)=μmg+2μN_A. Substituting N_A gives F=μmg+2μmg cosθ/(cosθ-μsinθ)=μmg(3cosθ-μsinθ)/(cosθ-μsinθ).
